method.scope: Current first-party employer role pages, employer-controlled job boards, official occupational data, and official role guidance.
method.source_policy: Primary sources only for material role claims; no job aggregators or third-party role summaries.
method.currentness_note: Job postings are volatile snapshots. Durable conclusions require convergence across employers, industries, and role families rather than reliance on one posting.

sources.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) - Seattle
sources.evidence_summary: Defines FDE as customer-partnered, end-to-end production deployment ownership spanning discovery, scoping, design, build, rollout, adoption, measurable workflow impact, and field feedback into product and model roadmaps.
sources.limitations: Frontier-model employer; its AI/evaluation emphasis is not universal to every FDE role.

sources.title: OpenAI careers search - forward deployed
sources.evidence_summary: Shows a named Forward Deployed Engineering function across many countries, plus distinct FDE, forward-deployed software, platform, security, technical deployment lead, management, government, and life-sciences variants.
sources.limitations: Open requisition counts and titles change frequently.

sources.title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Describes Palantir's pioneering FDSE model: engineers embed with customers, rapidly understand difficult problems, and architect and build solutions using business-critical data and AI.
sources.limitations: Uses the narrower FDSE title and is shaped by Palantir's platforms and deployment model.

sources.title: Palantir open roles
sources.evidence_summary: Shows a large, international forward-deployed role family spanning commercial, government, autonomous systems, infrastructure, reliability, security, enablement, internships, and seniority levels.
sources.limitations: Catalog reflects one employer and changes as requisitions open and close.

sources.title: Deployment Strategist, Internship
sources.evidence_summary: Separates strategist work—problem synthesis, workflow discovery, analytics, training, executive communication, demos, and engagement scoping—from FDE work integrating data into stable, extensible pipelines.
sources.limitations: Internship description, though it explicitly describes the full role and collaboration boundary.

sources.title: Forward Deployed Engineer - AI Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Places FDE inside Applied AI and assigns technical strategy and delivery of agentic systems from customer discovery through production launch.
sources.limitations: Early-stage AI company; role breadth may exceed mature-team boundaries.

sources.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Requires production-grade code, end-to-end discovery-to-rollout ownership, cloud/VPC/on-prem deployment, and resolution of security, networking, compliance, integration, and performance constraints.

sources.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Frames FDE as direct customer platform deployment and integration, including environments, large-scale data pipelines, training/evaluation frameworks, and production readiness.
sources.limitations: Model-training infrastructure context; not representative of application-only deployments.

sources.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Assigns ownership from sales handoff to stable production, including success criteria, UAT, go-live, training, workflow translation, production diagnostics, and decisions about agentic, deterministic, and human-review controls.
sources.limitations: Founding-role scope blends implementation, customer success, and process design.

sources.title: Founding Forward Deployed Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Makes the FDE technical owner of strategic customer relationships, production integrations, go-live and beyond; requires testing, staging, deployment safety, and converting field patterns into broader platform capability.
sources.limitations: Founding role with unusually broad account ownership.

sources.title: Unique paths to rewarding solutions architect careers at AWS
sources.evidence_summary: Defines the solutions architect as a blend of technical expertise, business acumen, customer advisory, and solution guidance using AWS services.

sources.title: Maximizing your cloud journey: Engaging an AWS Solutions Architect
sources.evidence_summary: Describes solutions architects as customer advocates and advisors who engage support or professional services/partners when hands-on infrastructure implementation is required.
sources.limitations: One provider's operating model; some solutions architects elsewhere write more implementation code.

sources.title: Software Developers - 15-1252.00
sources.organization: O*NET OnLine, U.S. Department of Labor
sources.evidence_summary: Defines the broad software-developer occupation around research, design, development, testing, maintenance, requirements, performance, and installation; customer consultation exists but is not the occupation's organizing lifecycle.
sources.limitations: FDE is not a separately classified O*NET occupation; occupational data is broader and slower-moving than employer roles.

sources.title: Anthropic careers - Applied AI roles
sources.evidence_summary: Shows Applied AI Engineer, Applied AI Architect, Partner Solutions Architect, and Solutions Architect as distinct named roles, supporting separation of engineering and architecture/advisory tracks.
sources.limitations: The catalog is highly volatile; an FDE role appeared in recent indexed snapshots but was not relied on as current duty evidence.

claims.statement: The durable FDE role anchor is direct work with customer/domain teams on complex real-world deployments, not internal product development alone.
FDEs commonly own a technical lifecycle from discovery and scoping through architecture, implementation, rollout, and stable production.
Production-grade coding, integration, testing, diagnostics, and remediation are core—not optional demonstration work.
Success is judged by adoption, workflow impact, go-live quality, and production stability rather than delivery of architecture documents alone.
Forward Deployed Engineer is a durable standalone title and role family, with Forward Deployed Software Engineer as a common narrower alias.
Employers distinguish FDE from platform, security, deployment-lead, architecture, and applied-AI roles even when they collaborate closely.
Customer-environment constraints make security, privacy, networking, compliance, governance, and human oversight part of deployment engineering decisions.
FDE work includes stakeholder alignment, adoption, training or enablement, and explicit success criteria alongside engineering delivery.
AI, model evaluation, and data pipelines are important current FDE contexts but are specializations of the deployment role rather than a universal definition of it.
A mature FDE converts repeated field lessons into reusable tools, playbooks, components, and product-roadmap feedback.
Solutions architecture overlaps in discovery and design but is commonly anchored in technical advisory and solution guidance rather than direct ownership of production implementation.

Software, ML, and data engineering capabilities support FDE execution, but their general occupational centers are systems or specialist technical assets rather than the customer deployment engagement.
Adjacent roles may share the same project while owning different primary decisions: problem/adoption, architecture/advice, specialist systems, or end-to-end deployed outcome.
FDE is an employer-defined emerging specialization rather than a separately standardized occupation in the current O*NET taxonomy.
